question.text: A stock's portfolio risk (σp) is ALWAYS <= weighted average risk (Σwi·σi) when correlations are:

explanation.text: The Logic: Strict inequality σp < Σwi·σi holds when ALL correlations < 1. Equality only when ρ = 1 everywhere. Diversification benefit is guaranteed as long as ρ < 1. The Trap: Students miss this key inequality. Cross-Exam Context: MPT result. Manager's Pro-Tip: This is why 'just hold more stocks' works even with moderate correlations — the math is on your side.
